promises.promise: Guarantee minimum income of Rs 72,000 per year to poorest families (NYAY scheme)

evidence_articles.title: Congress promises ₹72,000 per annum to poorest people
evidence_articles.rephrased: The article covers Rahul Gandhi's announcement of the NYAY minimum income guarantee scheme, which promises to directly transfer ₹72,000 per year to the bank accounts of India's poorest 20% families.
evidence_articles.content: Congress president Rahul Gandhi on Monday announced a minimum income guarantee scheme, Nyuntam Aay Yojana (NYAY), under which ₹72,000 a year will be transferred to the bank accounts of 20% of the poorest families in the country if his party is voted to power.

recent_articles.title: Mob attacks Trinamool leader Abhishek Banerjee; Mamata blames it on BJP - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Abhishek Banerjee**, general secretary of the **Trinamool Congress**, was attacked by a mob in Sonarpur, West Bengal on Saturday. The attack occurred during his visit to the residence of a party worker allegedly killed in post-poll violence.  The mob threw eggs and shoes at **Banerjee** as security personnel attempted to shield him from the crowd chanting "chor chor" (thief thief).

recent_articles.title: D.K. Shivakumar meets Governor Gehlot, stakes claim to form new govt in Karnataka - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **D.K. Shivakumar**, the newly elected leader of the **Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee**, will be sworn in as Chief Minister on Wednesday, June 3rd at Lok Bhavan. The event is expected to be attended by the central leadership of the party and Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot has invited him to take the oath at 4:05 p.m.  The power transition was overseen by **Mallikarjun Kharge**, **Rahul Gandhi**, and **Sonia Gandhi**.  With Cabinet formation still under discussion, speculation remains about whether a full Cabinet will be sworn in and if there will be deputy Chief Ministers.

recent_articles.title: Is Melania Trump an 'alien'? Indian-origin attorney says White House's immigrant-bashing crosses line - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rahul Reddy**, an Indian-origin immigration attorney, criticized the use of the word "alien" by **the White House**, arguing that it is dehumanizing and fuels negative perceptions.  He pointed out that while the term is legal in immigration law, its usage by the White House creates a narrative that paints lawful immigrants as outsiders. Reddy questioned if **Melania Trump**, who was born in Slovenia, is also an alien, highlighting the hypocrisy of using such language when the President's own family has a history of immigration.

recent_articles.title: Ponguleti lays stone for integrated sub-registrar office complex at Banjara Hills - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy**, **Revenue Minister of Andhra Pradesh**, laid the foundation stone for an Integrated Sub-Registrar Office complex in Banjara Hills. The project, expected to be completed within a few months, will combine offices from 13 Sub-Registrar units and other related departments under one roof.  The complex is being built by reputed private firms to improve public access and service delivery while generating employment and boosting business activity in the area.

recent_articles.title: ‘Super corruption government’ is coming to exist: Chalavadi Narayanaswamy - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chalavadi Narayanaswamy**, leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Council, criticized the **BJP** for its handling of the dissolved government, alleging that corruption persists despite the change. He stated that officers continue to engage in corrupt practices and development projects remain stalled, emphasizing the need for systemic changes rather than superficial leadership shifts.  Narayanaswamy also accused the Congress of neglecting Dalits and failing to nominate a Dalit as Chief Minister.

recent_articles.title: Congress govt. in Himachal changing election rules to hijack local body polls: BJP State chief - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rajeev Bindal**, **BJP Himachal Pradesh President**, accused the **Congress government** of attempting to manipulate urban local body and Panchayati Raj elections in the state. He claimed that the government amended election rules, granting deputy commissioners discretionary authority over meeting timings, and delaying the elections. Bindal argued this is an attempt to gain control over municipal councils and other bodies through political influence and money power, violating democratic principles and electoral laws.

recent_articles.title: D.K. Shivakumar to be sworn-in as Karnataka chief minister at Glass House in Lok Bhavan on June 3 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **D.K. Shivakumar**, the newly elected chief minister of Karnataka, will have his swearing-in ceremony at **Glass House** in **Bengaluru** on June 3rd.  **G.C. Chandrashekar**, **KPCC Working President**, stated that the decision to hold a simple oath-taking ceremony was made by the **Congress Legislative Party (CLP)** and that party workers are not required to attend. The event follows intense negotiations in New Delhi regarding power distribution among factions, with the CLP meeting scheduled for May 30th.

recent_articles.title: Tirthahalli co-op society president claims inquiry based on false complaints by loan defaulters - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Basavani Vijay Dev**, president of the Sahyadri Multipurpose Arecanut Growers’ Marketing Cooperative Society, alleges that the **Karnataka government** ordered inquiries into three Tirthahalli-based co-operative societies based on misleading information. The inquiries were prompted by complaints filed by loan defaulters who are now making false allegations against the societies.  Mr. Vijay Dev maintains his society has always been transparent and shares documents with shareholders, while initiating recovery proceedings against defaulting members.

recent_articles.title: Police arrests former MLA Balka Suman from Telangana Bhavan - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Balka Suman**, a former MLA of **Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS)**, was arrested by **Hyderabad police** from Telangana Bhavan on Saturday. Police had registered a case against him after he allegedly made remarks during a meeting at the party headquarters on May 26.  Suman accused the Congress government of targeting Opposition leaders through criminal cases before his arrest and an anticipatory bail petition was filed on his behalf. The police have not yet issued a detailed statement regarding the arrest, but further legal proceedings are expected in the case.

recent_articles.title: Claims of being vishwaguru but can't conduct single exam: Rahul's dig at PM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rahul Gandhi**, leader of the **Congress**, criticized **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** for the delayed CUET-UG 2026 examination, alleging that the government has destroyed the education system.  He accused **Modi** of being unable to conduct even a single examination properly despite claiming to be a "vishwaguru." **Gandhi** stated that this failure is impacting millions of students and will hold **Modi** accountable for his actions.

recent_articles.title: ‘Technical glitch’ delays CUET-UG 2026 exam at some centres - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The National Testing Agency (NTA)** announced a delay of over two hours for the first shift of the Common University Entrance Test-Undergraduate (CUET-UG) on Saturday, May 30, 2026, due to technical glitches at some examination centres. **Tata Consultancy Services (TCS)** was blamed for the delay, which affected candidates across different states. The NTA stated that the issue has been resolved and compensatory time will be provided to all candidates.  The second shift of the exam was also revised with entry starting at 1 p.m. and the examination beginning at 4 p.m.

recent_articles.title: Spurious liquor kills 15 in Pune, Pimpri-Chinchwad; 8 held, probe ordered - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: At least 15 people have died in Pune and Pimpri-Chinchwad after consuming spurious liquor, prompting an investigation by **Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis** and the **Excise Department**.  **Yogesh Wankhede**, who brought ethanol without permission, is suspected of preparing the illicit alcohol at a location in Hadapsar before supplying it to vendors. The deaths occurred over three days, with residents expressing anger towards authorities for allegedly failing to prevent the sale of illegal liquor.  The investigation is ongoing and more arrests are expected.

recent_articles.title: Congress holds talks with Hemant Soren on fielding party nominee from one of 2 Rajya Sabha seats going to polls in Jharkhand - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **K. Raju**, **Hemant Soren**, and **Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka** met to discuss fielding a Congress candidate for the upcoming Rajya Sabha elections in Jharkhand.  The decision on who will represent the party is pending approval from the high command, with former State Congress president Rajesh Thakur and former Union Minister Subodh Kant Sahay considered frontrunners. The election will take place on June 18th.

recent_articles.title: US judge orders removal of Donald Trump's name from Kennedy Center, blocks closure plan - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A US federal judge ruled that the **Kennedy Center**'s board exceeded its authority by adding President Donald Trump's name to the institution and blocking plans for a yearslong renovation. Judge Christopher Cooper ordered the removal of all signage bearing Trump's name within 14 days, stating Congress is the only entity with the power to change the center's name. The judge also found that the board's decision to close the center was "ill-informed" and lacked adequate consideration for its statutory obligations during a shutdown.

recent_articles.title: PM’s silence on CBSE OSM controversy shows he cares more about his govt’s survival than students’ future: Rahul Gandhi - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rahul Gandhi**, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, criticized **COEMPT Edutek's** win of the Central Board of Secondary Education’s (CBSE) on-screen marking contract, alleging that tender norms were manipulated to favor the company.  He questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi's silence on the controversy and claimed that the contract was awarded despite technical requirements being relaxed for COEMPT. **Gandhi** also highlighted concerns about the evaluation system's flaws and urged an independent judicial probe into all contracts awarded to **COEMPT**.

recent_articles.title: Telangana Information Commission clears massive backlog - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Telangana State Information Commission (TGIC)** has disposed of 14,434 cases since its formation in May 2025, leaving 10,996 pending. The commission has processed nearly 1,200 cases per month and interacted with over 30,000 individuals involved in the RTI process during hearings.  **State Chief Information Commissioner (RTI) Chandrasekhar Reddy**, along with other commissioners, briefed **Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy** on the commission's activities and functioning. The commission also conducted awareness camps and completed an expenditure audit for the first time since its inception.

recent_articles.title: Shivakumar’s elevation as Karnataka CM poses existential challenge for JD(S) - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **H.D. Kumaraswamy** and **D.K. Shivakumar**, both members of the Vokkaliga community, are facing a potential political challenge as the change in leadership within Karnataka's Congress-led government raises concerns for the **Janata Dal (Secular)**. The party is considering possible decisions that could see **Kumaraswamy** return to full-time State politics, which some view as disadvantageous given his rivalry with **Shivakumar**.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka government formation LIVE: Congress to convene crucial CLP meeting at 4 p.m. on May 30 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Siddaramaiah**, after resigning as the chief minister of Karnataka, met with **Rahul Gandhi** at **Sonia Gandhi’s** residence. The meeting focused on his future role within the **Congress** party and included discussions about his son's potential positions in the new government.  **Siddaramaiah** also met with **Mallikarjun Kharge**, the Congress chief, to discuss the transition process.

recent_articles.title: Internal bickering, resignations and public anger, Trinamool battling on multiple fronts - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Trinamool Congress** continues to face internal turmoil following its electoral defeat in West Bengal.  Senior MPs **Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar** and **Kalyan Banerjee** engaged in a public dispute, while senior MP **Sougata Roy** faced protests and alleged attacks from BJP supporters.  The party also saw the arrest of **Baduria municipality chairperson Dipankar Bhattacharya**, who was allegedly found with over ₹2.24 crore hidden in a jute field.  Former Rajya Sabha MP **Santanu Sen** resigned, criticizing the party's handling of the RG Kar rape and murder case.  **Mamata Banerjee** shared a cryptic poem on social media, while **Kunal Ghosh** urged party leaders to focus on internal solutions.

recent_articles.title: Global Market Today: Asian stocks rise on US-Iran truce deal, oil drops - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **MSCI Asia Pacific Index** rose 0.7% on Friday, fueled by optimism toward artificial intelligence and a potential ceasefire extension in the Iran-Saudi Arabia conflict. **Dell Technologies Inc.** surged after strong sales outlook, while **Brent crude** prices fell slightly.  The yen remained steady against the dollar, with US Treasury yields falling across the curve. Despite concerns about inflation, investors remain optimistic about a resolution to the Iran conflict and continued growth in the tech sector.

recent_articles.title: Revanth Reddy hails NTR as a leader beyond politics - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy** unveiled a statue of **N.T. Rama Rao**, praising him as a great leader who inspired significant change in people's lives through his policies.  **Reddy** highlighted the influence of **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, Indira Gandhi, and N.T. Rama Rao** on Indian history, emphasizing that their contributions empower the underprivileged. He noted that **NTR** abolished the 'Patel Patwari' system, empowered women in property rights, and introduced several prominent leaders from Telangana.  **Reddy** also cited **NTR's** ₹2-per-kg rice scheme as inspiration for the state's subsidized fine rice scheme.

recent_articles.title: Revanth should tender resignation: BJP - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **A. Maheshwar Reddy**, BJP Legislature Party leader, criticized **Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy** for failing to address farmers' crop procurement woes during a party tour in Telangana. He alleged that the government has not fulfilled any promises made to farmers and is prioritizing real estate over governance.  **Maheshwar Reddy** stated that less than 40% of grain had been procured, with produce rotting in threshing yards, leaving farmers distressed. The BJP will continue to pressure the government to address their concerns.

recent_articles.title: Ministers visit paddy procurement centre, ask officials to speed up purchase - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **N. Uttam Kumar Reddy**, the **Minister for Civil Supplies and Irrigation** of Telangana, visited procurement centers to assess damage caused by recent unseasonal rains on paddy stock.  He assured farmers that the government would continue procuring paddy without disruption and ensure they receive the Minimum Support Price (MSP). The government has procured 58 lakh tonnes of paddy so far and expects another 18 lakh tonnes to arrive in the coming days. **Mr. Uttam Kumar Reddy** also instructed officials to intensify lifting operations, improve storage arrangements, and strengthen coordination between departments to prevent delays in transportation.

recent_articles.title: Before relinquishing office, Siddaramaiah demolishes long-held myth linking Chamarajanagar visits to a Chief Minister’s fall from power - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Siddaramaiah**, Karnataka's longest-serving Chief Minister, visited Chamarajanagar town despite a long-held superstition that visiting the district would lead to power loss.  He consistently defied the belief, having visited the region multiple times during his two terms as Chief Minister and even convening a Cabinet meeting there last year. **Siddaramaiah** dismissed the superstition, stating he had no faith in it and that his political position had strengthened after each visit.

recent_articles.title: Siddaramaiah and D.K. Shivakumar: A public bonhomie that never let up - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Despite internal tensions within the **Congress** in Karnataka, **Siddaramaiah** and **Shivakumar**, leaders of opposing factions, maintained a cordial public image.  They were seen discussing power transfer in Delhi and even embraced after **Siddaramaiah's** resignation. Their unity was evident throughout their tenure, with frequent appearances together and gestures of support for each other. The transition of power from **Siddaramaiah** to **Shivakumar**, though initially feared to be messy, unfolded smoothly.

recent_articles.title: Telangana CM moots unified card to extend benefits of welfare schemes - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **A. Revanth Reddy**, **Telangana** Chief Minister, directed officials to develop a unified card for welfare scheme benefits. The card will encompass details of individual beneficiaries from various departments and utilize artificial intelligence to analyze data and identify ineligible recipients. Officials are tasked with gathering information from different departments through a special drive, incorporating details of schemes like Aarogyasri Health Scheme, fee reimbursement, insurance coverage, and the upcoming insurance scheme.  The Chief Minister also instructed officials to study the Kerala government's approach for migrant workers in the Middle East.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka politics LIVE: Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah announces decision to step down at breakfast meeting with Ministers - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Siddaramaiah**, Karnataka's Chief Minister, announced his resignation during a breakfast meeting at his residence on May 28th. He informed his Cabinet colleagues that he had been asked to step down by the **Congress High Command**.  He will visit the Governor’s office and address a press conference later in the day. The Congress Legislative Party is expected to meet on Friday (May 29, 2026) to discuss the likely successor.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka CM Siddaramaiah announces decision to step down at breakfast meeting with Ministers - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Siddaramaiah**, the Chief Minister of Karnataka, announced his resignation from the post during a breakfast meeting at his residence on May 28th. He informed his Cabinet colleagues that he had been asked to step down by the **Congress High Command**.  The decision comes after speculation about his continuation and an offer of a Rajya Sabha seat from **Rahul Gandhi**, Leader of Opposition in Rajya Sabha, who requested him to pave the way for a new leader. The Governor, **Thaawarchand Gehlot**, is expected to meet with **Siddaramaiah** before accepting his resignation.

recent_articles.title: ED raids Pinarayi Vijayan's residences in CMRL-Exalogic case - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Enforcement Directorate (ED)** conducted raids on the residences of former Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan and his daughter, T. Veena, in Kannur and Thiruvananthapuram, alleging that her defunct firm received substantial monthly retainers from **Cochin Minerals and Rutile Limited (CMRL)** between 2017 and 2021 without rendering any tangible service. The raids triggered protests across the state, with CPI(M) activists allegedly vandalizing vehicles carrying ED officials.  The ED is verifying bank transactions of Ms. Veena while stating no incriminating documents were found at Mr. Vijayan's residence.

recent_articles.title: Reuters executive Simon Robinson expected to replace Justin Stevens as ABC news director | Australian Broadcasting Corporation | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Simon Robinson**, currently deputy to the editor-in-chief of **Reuters**, is expected to be appointed as news director of the **ABC** in coming days.  He will replace **Justin Stevens**, who resigned after four years, citing personal and professional reasons. **Hugh Marks**, managing director of the **ABC**, stated that Stevens felt it was time for a refresh and rejuvenation of the organization's output. The appointment comes as the **ABC** seeks to adapt to the changing media landscape.

recent_articles.title: T.N. Congress forms committee to look into allegations of anti-party activities - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **K. Jayakumar**, head of the **Tamil Nadu Congress Committee** fact-finding committee, announced an investigation into allegations of anti-party activities by party workers during the recent Assembly elections. The committee will investigate complaints and present a report in 60 days.  The AICC has empowered the committee to gather feedback from stakeholders and ensure such behavior doesn't occur in future. Some party leaders expressed skepticism about the committee's findings, questioning its effectiveness given past alliances with the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK).

recent_articles.title: Probe incidents of accused being paraded in underwear: APDR writes to West Bengal Human Rights Commission - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A civil rights organization, the **Association of Protection of Democratic Rights (APDR)**, has filed a complaint with the **West Bengal Human Rights Commission** alleging that police officers in Howrah district paraded two accused individuals in their underwear and vests. The APDR cites two incidents at Golabari and Sankrail police stations on May 24th and 25th respectively, where the accused were subjected to this treatment.  The organization argues that these actions violate human rights and are a form of "criminal force" by law enforcement.

recent_articles.title: Rate at which West Bengal tribunals restoring names of deleted electors proves genuine voters not allowed to vote: Prasenjit Bose - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Prasenjit Bose**, chairperson of the SIR Committee of West Bengal Pradesh Congress Committee, stated that appellate tribunals have restored the names of 4,043 electors (61%) from over 25 lakh appeals against deletions in West Bengal.  He emphasized that this evidence demonstrates how genuine voters were wrongfully deleted during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process. **Bose** also pointed out that while the Supreme Court upheld the SIR exercise in Bihar, a clear judicial forum for electors to challenge decisions is necessary. The SIR resulted in 27 lakh voters being excluded from West Bengal electoral rolls on April 7th, weeks before the Assembly polls, with significant deletions occurring in two Muslim-dominated districts.

recent_articles.title: Thirumavalavan calls upon VCK cadre to “let go and move on” - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Thol. Thirumavalavan**, founder of the **Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK)**, addressed supporters after DMK leaders criticized the party for joining the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam-led state government's Cabinet.  He explained that he made the decision to join the Cabinet based on assessments of potential vote shifts and alliances following the Assembly elections. **Thirumavalavan** acknowledged criticisms from some DMK leaders, but emphasized the VCK's contribution to the alliance over the past decade and urged supporters to focus on strengthening their party. He also stated that the VCK's vote share has been transferred to its alliance partners.

recent_articles.title: Will Siddaramaiah's breakfast with Cabinet colleagues on May 28 end with leadership change in Karnataka? - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Siddaramaiah**, the Chief Minister of Karnataka, has invited his Cabinet colleagues for a breakfast meeting on Thursday to address speculation about his future.  The Congress high command has asked him to move to the Rajya Sabha, paving the way for a leadership change. **Randeep Singh Surjewala**, the All India Congress Committee general secretary in charge of Karnataka, arrived in Bengaluru to facilitate the transition process. While some party members are pushing for his resignation, he has refused to comment on the matter and only stated that he will speak tomorrow.

recent_articles.title: Trinamool MLA arrested, several leaders quit party post - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Dilip Mondal**, a Trinamool Congress MLA from Bishnupur, was arrested by **West Bengal police** in Odisha on Wednesday (May 27, 2026) after days of evading arrest. The arrest follows an investigation into alleged threats against **BJP** workers during the West Bengal Assembly elections and a previous complaint filed against him.  The arrest marks the first time a sitting MLA has been apprehended by **West Bengal police**. This comes amidst a wave of arrests targeting local Trinamool Congress workers, including former Minister **Sujit Bose**, for their alleged involvement in corruption and post-poll violence. The situation is further complicated by mass resignations from Trinamool leaders, including senior leader **Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar** and several councillors.  The party's leadership is also facing criticism for the lack of a designated space for the Leader of Opposition, **Sovandeb Chattopadhyay**, in the West Bengal Assembly premises.

recent_articles.title: Congress urges ECI to defer SIR in Maharashtra; cites Ashadhi Wari, monsoon rains - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Opposition Congress** in Maharashtra requested the **Election Commission** to postpone the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls by a month. The party cited the annual pilgrimage, Ashadhi Wari, and potential heavy monsoon rains during the revision process as reasons for their request.  They argued that millions of warkaris participating in the pilgrimage may be absent from their homes during the second phase of the SIR program, potentially leading to voter exclusion.

recent_articles.title: Defiant Pinarayi Vijayan raises fist after ED raid, vows ‘long battle’ against BJP and Congress - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Pinarayi Vijayan**, former Kerala Chief Minister and now Leader of the Opposition, emerged from his residence in Thiruvananthapuram to greet hundreds of **CPI(M)** workers protesting against a seven-hour raid by the **Enforcement Directorate (ED)**.  He criticized the BJP for using central enforcement agencies to target opposition figures while accusing the Congress of tacitly supporting these actions.  **Mr. Vijayan** asserted that the Communist movement would not be deterred and vowed to fight for democracy and equality, despite the damage caused to vehicles by protesting party workers who were subsequently arrested.

recent_articles.title: Andhra Pradesh cannot afford YSRCP’s return in 2029, says Chandrababu Naidu at Mahanadu - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **N. Chandrababu Naidu**, leader of the **Telugu Desam Party (TDP)**, urged party members to adhere to "coalition dharma" and prevent the **YSR Congress Party (YSRCP)** from returning to power in 2029.  Naidu criticized the YSRCP's proposed capital development plan for the Machilipatnam-Vijayawada-Guntur region and highlighted the party's failures during its tenure, citing financial difficulties faced by the coalition government. He emphasized the TDP's commitment to welfare, development, and good governance over the years, highlighting its resilience against political challenges.

recent_articles.title: CM for enabling panchayats to credit their own source revenue in bank accounts - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Chief Minister of Telangana**, A. Revanth Reddy, announced reforms aimed at strengthening **Panchayat Raj institutions**. These include allowing gram panchayats to deposit their own revenue into separate bank accounts and ensuring timely salary payments to over 50,000 village panchayat staff. The government will also release ₹50 crore monthly for this purpose.  The reforms are intended to revive the independence of gram panchayats and streamline pension disbursement processes.

recent_articles.title: Taint of defection is not vaporised by resignation, Supreme Court had said in a judgment - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: In Tamil Nadu, the Speaker has accepted resignations from four AIADMK legislators who joined the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) after voting against the ruling coalition. The **AIADMK** leadership is appealing to the Speaker to reconsider their acceptance and adjudicate on petitions for their disqualification. This situation raises questions about the Speaker's role in accepting resignations while pending disqualification proceedings, as seen in a 2019 Supreme Court case where the court ruled that the Speaker cannot consider extraneous factors when evaluating a resignation.  The outcome of this case will likely impact the fate of these legislators and their ability to hold office.

recent_articles.title: Leadership tussle in Karnataka: Congress high command wants Siddaramaiah to move to Rajya Sabha, sources say, even as party officially denies - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Siddaramaiah**, the current Chief Minister of **Karnataka**, is facing pressure to step down after a meeting with the **Congress** high command in New Delhi. The discussions centered on selecting candidates for Rajya Sabha and Legislative Council elections, but sources suggest that leadership change was also a key topic.  Despite official denials, there are indications that the party may be considering a shift in leadership if **Siddaramaiah** doesn't agree to step down.  The high command is facing pressure to make a decision before June 8th deadline for Rajya Sabha nominations.

recent_articles.title: Mundamveli residents lay day-long siege to GCDA headquarters - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Residents of the P&T Apartment Complex in Mundamveli protested at the **Greater Cochin Development Authority (GCDA)** headquarters on Tuesday, demanding a probe into alleged violations of distance norms from an 110 kV EHT line. The residents, who moved into the twin towers built by the GCDA in January 2024, have been facing electrical problems and leakage issues since moving in. **Kochi MLA Mohammed Shiyas** visited the protest site and promised to petition the Chief Minister for a Vigilance probe.  The GCDA maintains that the apartments were constructed with all necessary permissions but acknowledged the need to address the residents' concerns about the safety of the structures.

recent_articles.title: Himachal panchayat polls: 78.53% polling in first phase, women voters outnumber men - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Over 78% of eligible voters participated in the first phase of Himachal Pradesh's panchayat elections, with women voters exceeding men in turnout. The highest voter participation was recorded in Kullu district at 84.43%, while Lahaul and Spiti had the lowest turnout at 69.40%.  The State Election Commission reported peaceful voting conditions across the state, with some minor issues such as a missing candidate's name on ballot papers leading to cancellations or postponements. The elections are being held in three phases, with results expected for various positions by May 31st.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka: Biennial polls to 7 Council seats from Assembly on June 18 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Election Commission of India** announced that biennial elections for seven council seats in Karnataka will be held on June 18. The notification for the elections will be issued on June 1, with nominations filing beginning then and ending on June 11.  Polls will take place on June 18, followed by vote counting on the same day. The last day for completing the election process is June 20. This follows the retirement of seven **MLCs** from the Legislative Council on June 30.

recent_articles.title: Leader of Opposition R. Ashok criticises Congress government - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **R. Ashok**, the **Opposition Leader in the Legislative Assembly**, criticized the **Congress party's** internal power struggle, stating that it has rendered the Karnataka government dysfunctional. He claimed that most ministers are in Delhi while the state administration lacks direction, and the high command is ineffective in restoring order.  **Siddaramaiah**, the Chief Minister of Karnataka, faces accusations of accumulating excessive debt through "unscientific and fiscally irresponsible guarantee schemes," according to **Ashok**.

recent_articles.title: CM Vijay to fly to New Delhi on Wednesday, to call on PM Modi - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **C. Joseph Vijay**, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister, will travel to New Delhi on Wednesday to meet **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**.  He plans to discuss issues including financial matters and the **Mekedatu** reservoir project with **Modi**.  **Vijay** is also expected to meet with Union Ministers and may meet with **Rahul Gandhi**.

recent_articles.title: First Taiwan, then South Korea? How global AI supercycle is demoting Indian stock market - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Taiwan’s** market capitalization reached $4.95 trillion, surpassing **India’s** value of $4.92 trillion, driven by the surge in **Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.** (TSMC). recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rahul Gandhi** attended the swearing-in ceremony of **C. Joseph Vijay**, the new Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, on Sunday (May 10, 2026). However, despite the Congress's request for both of its MLAs to be sworn in as Cabinet Ministers at the same time, the **Tamil Nadu Vettri Kazhagam** (TVK) opted to delay the swearing-in. The TVK is planning to include members from other coalition partners like the AIADMK in the cabinet expansion.  The decision not to immediately swear in the Congress MLAs was seen as a missed opportunity by some party leaders who felt it would have sent a strong message of unity.

recent_articles.title: CM selection a democratic process: Chennithala - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Ramesh Chennithala**, a senior Congress leader, criticized the BJP for its alleged delay in selecting a Chief Minister after the 2025 Delhi Assembly elections. He defended the **Congress**'s democratic process and emphasized that decisions are made through discussions within the party.  Chennithala stated that five days is not an unreasonable time frame for such a decision, especially considering the complexity of the selection process. The Congress leadership has been meeting with various leaders to arrive at a consensus on the next Chief Minister.

recent_articles.title: ​No detours: On the Tamil Nadu elections, post-poll outcome - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)**, led by C. Joseph Vijay, formed a government after securing the support of **Congress**, **CPI(M)**, **CPI**, **VCK**, and **IUML** parties, despite falling short of a majority. The Governor's decision to disregard the Sarkaria Commission framework and Supreme Court rulings regarding the strength of a ministry was criticized.  The Congress's alliance with the TVK is seen as opportunistic, potentially jeopardizing their decades-long alliance with the DMK.

recent_articles.title: Suvendu Adhikari to chair first Cabinet meeting on May 11, 2026 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, the newly elected Chief Minister of **West Bengal**, will hold his first cabinet meeting on Monday, May 11, at Nabanna.  The meeting will see the allocation of portfolios to five ministers who were sworn in with him on Saturday. The cabinet is expected to establish inquiry commissions into atrocities against women during the **Trinamool Congress** regime. Adhikari also plans to meet with top officials from various departments including the police and district magistrates.

recent_articles.title: I-PAC emerges as Trinamool’s fall guy after West Bengal Assembly poll debacle - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Trinamool Congress** leaders are blaming **I-PAC**, a political consultancy firm, for the party's loss in the 2026 West Bengal Assembly elections. Senior leader **Kalyan Banerjee** stated that the reliance on **I-PAC** had detrimental effects on the party's organization and that **Abhishek Banerjee's** dependence on the firm was not well received.

recent_articles.title: Kerala’s fiscal worries - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **V.D. Satheesan**, the **Kerala** Opposition Leader, claims that the newly elected **UDF** government inherited a nearly empty treasury from the **LDF**.  The new government faces challenges in managing Kerala's finances, including high expenditures on salaries, pensions, and interest payments, limited tax revenue potential, and the impact of the 16th Finance Commission awards. The outgoing Finance Minister, **K.N. Balagopal**, disputes these claims, emphasizing that the state is in a better financial position than it was under the previous government.  The new government will need to address these challenges to fulfill its promises of development and social welfare programs.

recent_articles.title: Congress claims Instagram blocked Rahul Gandhi's reel and photo post featuring Vijay due to MeitY rules - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** leader Rahul Gandhi's post featuring him and actor-politician Vijay after the Tamil Nadu chief minister's oath-taking ceremony was mistakenly flagged for blocking by **Instagram**, according to **Congress** aide Srivatsa.  He claimed that the action is due to Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) rules, but **MeitY** sources denied this, stating it was a platform error. The post had garnered millions of views before being restored.
